exact_prompt:
I'm shopping for cottage cheese in the United States.

Which brand should I buy, and why?
reviewed_answer:
When shopping for cottage cheese in the United States, a few standout brands dominate the market for different reasons. Depending on what you value most—flavor, clean ingredients, or price—here are the best choices to look for:

1. Best Overall: Good Culture

Why buy it: Good Culture has developed a massive cult following among food critics and cottage cheese lovers alike, frequently topping taste tests across major food publications.

The Taste & Texture: It features exceptionally thick, creamy, and velvety whole milk or low-fat options with a pleasant, mild tang. It avoids the watery, soupy texture that plagues lower-quality brands.   

Health Perks: It is packed with protein (around 14 grams per half-cup), is lower in sodium than many legacy brands, and includes live and active probiotic cultures. Their organic lines use pasture-raised milk with minimal, clean ingredients (no gums or thickeners).   

2. Best Classic & Minimal Ingredients: Daisy

Why buy it: If you want a traditional, no-fuss cottage cheese with a century-old reputation for quality, Daisy is the gold standard.   

The Taste & Texture: Daisy is famous for its simple ingredient list—just milk, cream, salt, and active cultures, with no gums, stabilizers, or added starches. It has a bright, clean, slightly tart flavor and a phenomenal, balanced curd texture.   

Health Perks: Highly reliable nutrition profile with high protein and reasonable sodium levels. It's widely available in almost every grocery store across the country.   

3. Best Budget Options: Trader Joe's or Aldi (Friendly Farms) or Walmart (Great Value)

Why buy it: If you eat cottage cheese regularly and want great quality without paying premium prices, private-label store brands punch way above their weight.

The Taste & Texture:

Trader Joe's Small Curd: Praised for having a neutral, highly versatile flavor that pairs effortlessly with either sweet (fruit/honey) or savory (pepper/tomatoes) toppings.   

Aldi (Friendly Farms): Highly rated for offering great texture and a classic tangy bite at a fraction of the cost.

Walmart (Great Value): Frequently scores high in national blind taste tests for its creamy blend and excellent versatility, produced by major dairy suppliers.

Quick Buying Tips:

Curd Size: Choose small curd if you prefer a smoother, more uniform texture or plan to blend it into smoothies, dips, or baking. Choose large curd if you enjoy a meatier, chunkier bite.

Fat Content: 4% milkfat (Whole Milk) is much richer and creamier, while 1% or 2% (Low-Fat) cuts back on calories while still offering a great protein punch.

Are you planning to eat it plain, use it in baking or smoothies, or pair it with specific sweet or savory toppings?
